item.title: A Coming Revolution in American Democracy
item.dc:creator: Rob Richie
item.description:
Barn Raiser

Americans’ celebration of 250 years of independence invites reflection on the Declaration of Independence and its values of equality, liberty and democratic renewal. Those values are a beacon to guide where our nation must go to live up to its promise—to make sure we have a democracy where your vote counts no matter how much money you have or where you live. We have work to do. Democracy is under profound stress. item.title: Young Candidates and Organizers Pave the Way for Rural Civic Engagement
item.dc:creator: Delanie Seals
item.description:
Barn Raiser

Running for office and organizing in Oklahoma is tough, but even tougher as a young person organizing in rural Oklahoma. With a total population of nearly 4 million across 77 counties, roughly 36% of Oklahoma residents live in rural areas. Oklahoma’s median age is 37, below the national average, and many younger folks play a role in politics, often behind the scenes. In 2023, the average age of Oklahoma legislators was 52, with 11 out of 149 legislators under the age of 35. item.title: Voters Reject Farm Bureau Push to Limit Citizen Amendments
item.dc:creator: Clayton Steward
item.description:
Barn Raiser

On August 4, Missourians overwhelmingly rejected a state constitutional amendment that would have limited the ability of voters to pass citizen-led amendments. The Missouri Farm Bureau strongly backed Amendment 4, which would have required any citizen-led ballot measure to obtain a majority vote in each of Missouri’s eight congressional districts, instead of the current requirement of a simple majority of all voters in the state. item.title: Some Establishment Democrats Want to Ban Ranked-Choice Voting
item.dc:creator: Rob Richie
item.description:
Barn Raiser

This Saturday, at their summer meeting in Austin, Texas, members of the Democratic National Committee (DNC) will likely get a chance to vote on whether the Democratic Party should ban the use of ranked choice voting (RCV) in selecting their presidential nominee in 2028. item.title: Deere Settlement Is a Win for the Right to Repair. But Advocates Say There’s a Catch
item.dc:creator: Miranda Lipton
item.description:
Barn Raiser

After years of pressure from farmers, independent repair shops and right-to-repair advocates, John Deere has agreed to a proposed $99 million settlement with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and five state attorneys general that would require the company to make many of its repair tools, software and documentation available beyond its authorized dealer network. The July 8 agreement marks a federal victory for the right-to-repair movement, as it promises to lower repair costs and reduce downtime for farmers.
